title: If it rains, we’ll stay in
goal: Talk about real possibilities with if
intro: For facts that are always true, use present + present: “If you heat ice, it melts.” For real possibilities in the future, use if + present, then will: “If it rains, we’ll stay in.” Never put “will” in the if-half.

examples: If I drink coffee late, I can’t sleep.
If you press this, the light turns on.

rules.rule: Real future: if + present, will + verb.
examples: If you leave now, you’ll catch the train.
If she calls, I’ll tell her.

rules.rule: The if-half can come first (with a comma) or second.
examples: I’ll help you if you ask.
If you ask, I’ll help you.

mistakes.wrong: If you will come, I will be happy.
mistakes.right: If you come, I’ll be happy.

mistakes.wrong: If it will rain, the match will stop.
mistakes.right: If it rains, the match will stop.

mistakes.wrong: If I will get time, I will call.
mistakes.right: If I get time, I’ll call.

mistakes.wrong: If you heat water, it will boils.
mistakes.right: If you heat water, it boils.

ex.q: If you ___ now, you’ll be on time.
If I see him, I ___ him your message.
If you mix red and white, you ___ pink.
We’ll go to the beach if the weather ___ good.
If you will need help, call me.
ex.fixed: If you need help, call me.

ex.q: If she will study, she will pass.
ex.fixed: If she studies, she will pass.

ex.q: If I finish early, I come to your place.
ex.fixed: If I finish early, I will come to your place.

ex.q: If it ___ (rain) tomorrow, we’ll cancel the trip.

ex.a: If you need anything, just call me.

ex.q: Correct this: “If I will get the job, I will buy a car.”
a: If I get the job I will buy a car
If I get the job I'll buy a car

talk: Talk about your plans for next month with “if”: If I get time…, If the weather is good…, If I save enough….
